item.title: [Palace Films] GOODBYE CRUEL WORLD - Official HD Trailer - Only In Cinemas
item.description:
http://www.palacefilms.com.au/goodbye-cruel-world © Palace Films

CLOSING NIGHT SELECTION – 2026 CANNES FILM FESTIVAL (Critics’ Week)

After starring in Mia Hansen-Love’s 'Eden' and producing and co-writing the Oscar-nominated 'Arco', the multi-talented Félix de Givry makes his hugely accomplished directorial debut with this delicate and moving romantic fable following the unlikely love story between two lonely teenagers.

14-year-old idealist Otto Vidal ('Anatomy of a Fall’ breakout Milo Machado-Graner) has decided he has no place in the world. After years of being bullied and humiliated, he posts farewell letters to his mother and classmates and disappears, forcing his small Normandy town to grieve a boy it believes is gone... even if he isn’t. Several nights later, Otto is recognised lurking in the town outskirts by Léna (Jane Beever), a shy classmate who, rather than give him up, impulsively chooses to shelter him in a spare room at her mother’s guesthouse. A tender, secret bond slowly grows between these two solitary teens, both hovering between childhood and the adult lives that await them...

Gently echoing the French New Wave, with dreamy Super 16mm cinematography by Tara-Jay Bangalter (son of Daft Punk’s Thomas Bangalter) and an original melodic score by César Award-winner Arnaud Toulon, GOODBYE, CRUEL WORLD beautifully captures the intense emotions of being young and invisible, and the tentative, transformative hope that comes when someone finally sees you.

item.title: [Palace Films] THE FIRES - Official HD Trailer - Only In Cinemas
item.description:
© Palace Films

WINNER (x6!) - 2026 ICELANDIC FILM AWARDS - incl. Best Production Design, Visual Effects and Score

Adapted from the best-selling novel by Sigríður Hagalín Björnsdóttir, this breathtaking thriller directed and co-written by Ugla Hauksdóttir in her debut feature film follows a volcanologist facing two simultaneous disasters.

Anna Arnardóttir (Vigdís Hrefna Pálsdóttir) is Iceland's top volcanologist, but her growing concerns about an impending eruption after recurring earthquakes are downplayed by her colleagues who wish to keep citizens and visitors calm and avoid sparking panic.

Against the backdrop of a potential disaster, her life is upended by a romantic affair with the mysterious and attractive Danish photographer Thomas (Pilou Asbæk), who reinvigorates her stagnant love life, but also has the power to destroy her marriage.

As the tension escalates between Thomas and Anna, the volcanic activity also rises, until the safety of the capital city Reykjavík is threatened and in the dangerous moments before impending disaster, emotions begin to bubble over.

item.title: [Modern Films] Everybody Digs Bill Evans | Official UK Trailer
item.description:
Winner of the Silver Bear for Best Director at the 2026 Berlin Film Festival, Everybody Digs Bill Evans is a biographical drama film about the legendary jazz pianist and composer Bill Evans.

Directed by Grant Gee and starring Anders Danielsen Lie, Bill Pullman and Laurie Metcalf, the film is written by Mark O’Halloran and based on Owen Martell’s novel Intermission.

1961. Bill Evans is playing with what he considers the perfect musical trio until tragedy strikes in the premature death of his bass player, Scott LaFaro - his musical soulmate. Traumatised by grief, Evans stops playing for the first time since his childhood. A tug-of-war between personal torment and the seemingly safer haven of familial love will see Evans oscillate between New York and suburbia, his genius always bubbling beneath the surface.

DIRECTOR Grant Gee
CAST Anders Danielsen Lie, Bill Pullman, Laurie Metcalf, Barry Ward, Valene Kane

In UK and Irish cinemas September 11

item.title: [Palace Films] BUTTERFLY - Official HD Trailer - Only In Cinemas
item.description:
© Palace Films

The brilliant Renate Reinsve (‘The Worst Person in the World’, ‘Sentimental Value’, ‘Fjord’) leads Itonje Søimer Guttormsen’s BUTTERFLY, an intriguing and mystical drama about two estranged sisters who reunite in Gran Canaria after the sudden, mysterious death of their mother.

Half-sisters Diana (Helene Bjørneby) and Lily (Reinsve) grew up as the only resident children at an all-inclusive resort in the Canary Islands, where their uninhibited mother, Vera, worked as a tour guide. Twenty-five years later, they are estranged, having both actively sought distance from the island and from each other.

Forced back to the island together, they must confront the aftermath of Vera’s death at an esoteric mountain retreat, where she had tried to build a spiritual world far removed from the island’s package-tour veneer.

item.title: [Palace Films] THE LAST VIKING - Official HD Trailer - Only In Cinemas
item.description:
http://www.palacefilms.com.au/the-last-viking © Palace Films

WINNER – 2026 ROBERT (DANISH ACADEMY) AWARDS – Audience Award
OFFICIAL SELECTION – 2025 VENICE INTERNATIONAL FILM FESTIVAL
OFFICIAL SELECTION – 2025 TORONTO INTERNATIONAL FILM FESTIVAL

The great Mads Mikkelsen ('Another Round') and Nikolaj Lie Kaas ('Department Q') lean into the mayhem in the outrageous new black comedy from award-winning writer-director Anders Thomas Jensen ('Riders of Justice', 'Adam’s Apples'). It follows a bank robber who must unlock his brother’s lost memory to recover long-buried heist money.
Rural Denmark, present day.

Anker (Lie Kaas), a career criminal with dreams of a never-ending holiday somewhere sunny, is released from prison after a fifteen-year sentence. Before he was put away, Anker pressured his brother Manfred (Mikkelsen) to hide the stolen money near their mother’s home, and only Manfred knows where it is. But while Anker has been behind bars, Manfred has developed an alter ego - convinced he’s John Lennon - and has forgotten the money ever existed. With the help of a psychologist, the brothers set out to recover the loot, but their journey spirals into something far stranger - and more revealing - than they ever expected…

For all its outlandishness and unpredictability, THE LAST VIKING finds genuine empathy amidst the dark humour, emerging as a warm-hearted comedy about identity and how we’re shaped by the stories others tell about us, and the ones we choose for ourselves.

Directed and co-written by Maria Sødahl, THE LAST RESORT is an absorbing drama about a Danish family forced to reassess their moral compass during a dream holiday in the Canary Islands.

When Mikkel (Espen Smed) and Louise (Danica Ćurčić) set off on a well-deserved charter holiday with their two daughters, they have only one goal: to enjoy a carefree week together after a long stretch of everyday pressures. But beyond their all-inclusive bubble, another reality unfolds, as thousands arrive by sea in search of a better life. When they encounter a man in need, they choose to help. As his requests grow and their involvement deepens, their good intentions begin to give way to fear for their own safety.

item.title: [Palace Films] THE LOVE THAT REMAINS - Official HD Trailer - Only in Cinemas
item.description:
http://www.palacefilms.com.au/the-love-that-remains © Palace Films

From award-winning writer/director Hlynur Pálmason ('Godland', 'A White, White Day') – one of cinema’s most singular contemporary artists – THE LOVE THAT REMAINS tenderly and hilariously captures a year in the life of a family of five, as the parents navigate their separation.

Though in the throes of a splitting up, Anna (Saga Garðarsdóttir) and Magnus (Sverrir Gudnason) still spend time together for the sake of their three children, Ída and twins Þorgils and Grímur (played, remarkably, by the three real-life children of director Pálmason). Magnus works at sea, infrequently returning to land, where he asserts himself as the patriarch with limited efficacy. Anna is an artist whose vast and impressive works fail to receive suitable recognition. In their interactions, whilst there's sufficient indication of why the separation is happening, there's also the familiarity of a long-held love and a glimmer of a chance of reconciliation...

Often taking playful and laugh-out-loud diversions, Pálmason's deeply felt film conveys so much love for its characters and the gorgeous Icelandic environment, delivering a soulful look at the importance of family and shared memories amidst the changing seasons.


OFFICIAL SELECTION (ICELAND) - 2026 ACADEMY AWARDS - Best International Feature

item.title: [Palace Films] NARCISO - Official HD Trailer - Only In Cinemas
item.description:
http://www.palacefilms.com.au/narciso © Palace Films 2026

WINNER - 2026 BERLIN FILM FESTIVAL (Panorama) – FIPRESCI Prize for Best Film

Inspired by notorious real-life events, the seductive new noir from multi award-winning writer/director Marcelo Martinessi ('The Heiresses') unravels the mysterious death of a charismatic radio host in late-1950s Paraguay — as the rebellious pulse of rock ’n’ roll crackling over the airwaves sparks fear, scandal and a national moral panic.

Asunción, 1959. Under dictator Alfredo Stroessner’s tightening military regime, magnetic young DJ Narciso Arévalos (a captivating Diro Romero) is found dead after his provocative final broadcast. His popularity has risen in tandem with the arrival of imported American music, which Narciso – having returned from Buenos Aires energised by the likes of Chuck Berry and Buddy Holly - has convinced the station’s repressed owner Lulú (Manuel Cuenca) to play in place of traditional Paraguayan folk standards. Filmed live before an adoring crowd, Narciso’s show ignites a generation craving freedom. Yet his defiant allure also earns powerful, dangerous attention, and stirs envy among the fearful...

Visually stunning and immersive, Martinessi’s atmospheric thriller probes how desire, fear, and shared beliefs work together to sustain dictatorships. Sounding a warning from the past that resonates amid today’s authoritarian resurgence, NARCISO reminds us that few forces challenge conformity more powerfully than art — especially the electrifying sound of rock ’n’ roll.

item.description:
http://www.palacefilms.com.au/la-salsa-vive © Palace Films 2026

OFFICIAL SELECTION - 2026 SPANISH & LATIN AMERICAN FILM FESTIVAL
OFFICIAL SELECTION – 2025 SXSW FILM FESTIVAL

In the tradition of 'The Buena Vista Social Club', Juan Carvajal’s joyful debut LA SALSA VIVE ('Salsa Lives') is a vibrant cinematic exploration of a musical movement that has ignited generations, salsa, weaving stories from its origins in 1960s New York City, USA, to its contemporary thriving scene in Cali, Colombia.

Born from the rich, interwoven sounds of the Caribbean, salsa emerged in New York as a powerful cultural force, bringing dozens of Latin American musical traditions under one umbrella. As its popularity shifted over time, salsa found a fervent new home in Cali, where it continues to thrive with unmatched energy across dance schools, nightclubs, orchestras, and the city’s spirited neighbourhoods.

Blending remarkable archival footage, live recordings and illuminating interviews with legends including singers Rubén Blades and Henry Fiol, percussionists Samuel Formell and Johnny "Dandy" Rodríguez, and 100-year-old maestro Willie Rosario, LA SALSA VIVE captures both the history and enduring pulse of salsa. Celebrating devoted dancers, music collectors, and a new generation embracing its rhythms, the film - a smash hit at the Colombian box office - is an exhilarating love letter to a vivid and living cultural legacy.

item.title: [Palace Films] BERLIN HERO - Official HD Trailer - Only In Cinemas
item.description:
http://www.palacefilms.com.au/berlin-hero © Palace Films 2026

OPENING NIGHT SELECTION - 2026 GERMAN FILM FESTIVAL

The final film from Wolfgang Becker ('Good Bye, Lenin!'), completed shortly before his passing, BERLIN HERO is a sharp, bittersweet satire adapted from Maxim Leo’s 2022 novel about an ordinary man swept up in an extraordinary lie.

Berlin, 2019. As the city marks 30 years since the fall of the Wall, Micha Hartung (Charly Hübner) is barely getting by, running - and living in - a failing video store. But when a magazine journalist (Leon Ullrich) uncovers a long-forgotten incident from his past, everything changes. As a railway worker in the German Democratic Republic, Micha once mistakenly sent a train across the border into the West. Reimagined as a bold act of defiance, the story is spun into a media sensation, casting Micha as the mastermind behind the biggest mass escape in GDR history. Reluctant at first, Micha is soon caught in the glare of fame – which also has its perks, as he meets his dream woman, Paula (Christiane Paul). He never imagined an ordinary guy like him could attract someone so successful, educated and witty, but like the rest of his life, this budding love story threatens to descend into a chaos of miscommunication and lies.

Blending satire with emotional nuance, BERLIN HERO features a standout ensemble including Jürgen Vogel, Daniel Brühl, Thorsten Merten and Peter Kurth, delivering a distinctly German comedy with bite and charm.

item.title: [Palace Films] MY FRIEND EVA - Official HD Trailer - Only In Cinemas
item.description:
http://www.palacefilms.com.au/my-friend-eva © Palace Films 2026

The effervescent, crowd-pleasing new comedy from Cesc Gay ('Truman', 'A Gun In Each Hand', and 'The People Upstairs', which recently formed the basis for Olivia Wilde’s 'The Invite') stars a luminous Nora Navas ('Pain & Glory') as a middle-aged woman who dares to disrupt her carefully constructed life in pursuit of one last, intoxicating chance at romance.

On a business trip in Rome, Eva (Navas), on the cusp of turning 50, shares a fleeting but electric encounter with Argentine screenwriter Álex (Rodrigo de la Serna, 'The Motorcycle Diaries', 'Money Heist'). The connection rekindles something long dormant - desire, spontaneity, and the dizzying thrill of possibility. Back in Barcelona with her husband (Juan Diego Botto, 'The Room Next Door') and teenage children, Eva finds herself unable to return to the rhythms of her former life. As the pull of this unexpected awakening intensifies, Eva makes a radical choice that blindsides her family and friendships, forcing everyone around her to confront their own ideas of love, loyalty, and reinvention.

Witty, perceptive, and deeply humane, MY FRIEND EVA explores the pitfalls of choosing passion over stability, and the complicated, often comic realities of starting over when life is already well underway.

item.title: [Modern Films] Leonora in the Morning Light | Official UK Trailer
item.description:
Defiant, brilliant, and untamable, Leonora Carrington refused to live by anyone’s rules but her own. In the charged atmosphere of 1930s Paris, she falls under the spell of the Surrealist movement—and into a passionate, volatile love affair with the German artist Max Ernst. Together, they create a world where art and life blur, surrounded by icons like André Breton and Salvador Dalí, and build an otherworldly refuge in the south of France filled with sculpted creatures and strange, living dreams.

But as war engulfs Europe, their fantasy shatters. Ernst is arrested as an enemy alien, and Leonora is thrust into a nightmare of loss, madness, and survival. Fleeing to Spain, she spirals into psychological torment and endures brutal institutional treatment. Emerging scarred but unbroken, Leonora finds her way to Mexico—a place of magic and rebirth—where she reclaims her art, her identity, and her freedom.

Leonora in the Morning Light is the epic true story of a woman who turned trauma into transcendence, creating beauty from chaos and forging a legacy that changed the history of modern art.

DIRECTOR Thor Klein & Lena Vurma
CAST Olivia Vinall, Alexander Scheer, Cassandra Ciangherotti, Ryan Gage, Istvan Teglas, Luis Gerardo Mendez

In UK and Irish cinemas May 29

item.title: [Modern Films] Oslo Stories Trilogy: Sex | Official UK Trailer
item.description:
Premiered in Berlinale’s Panorama, Sex follows two men, both in heterosexual marriages, who have an unexpected experience that challenges their understanding of sexuality, gender, and identity. One has a sexual encounter with another man, without considering it either as an expression of homosexuality or infidelity, and discusses it with his wife afterwards. The other finds himself in nocturnal dreams where he is seen as a woman, stirring confusion and leading him to question how much his personality is shaped by the gaze of others.

Part of the OSLO STORIES TRILOGY: DREAMS LOVE SEX from director Dag Johan Haugerud.

CAST Gunnar Røise, Thorbjørn Harr, Siri Forberg, Birgitte Larsen

In UK and Irish cinemas August 22

item.title: [Modern Films] Oslo Stories Trilogy: Love | Official UK Trailer
item.description:
Premiered in Competition at the Venice Film Festival, Love follows Marianne, a pragmatic doctor, and Tor, a compassionate nurse, who are both avoiding conventional relationships. One evening, after a blind date, Marianne encounters Tor on the ferry. Tor, who often spends his nights there seeking casual encounters with men, shares his experiences of spontaneous intimacy. Intrigued by his perspective, Marianne begins to explore whether casual intimacy could also be an option for her.

Part of the OSLO STORIES TRILOGY: DREAMS LOVE SEX from director Dag Johan Haugerud.

CAST Andrea Bræin Hovig, Tayo Cittadella Jacobsen, Marte Engebrigtsen, Lars Jacob Holm, Thomas Gullestad, Marian Saastad Ottesen, Morten Svartveit

item.title: [Modern Films] Oslo Stories Trilogy: Dreams | Official UK Trailer
item.description:
Winner of the Golden Bear at the 2025 Berlin Film Festival, DREAMS follows Johanne as she falls in love for the first time, with her teacher. To preserve her feelings, she documents her emotions and experiences in writing. When her mother and grandmother read what she has written, they are initially shocked by its intimate content but soon see that it has literary potential. As they debate whether to publish it, Johanne navigates the gap between her romantic fantasy and reality, and all three women confront their differing views on love, sexuality, and self-discovery.

Part of the OSLO STORIES TRILOGY: DREAMS LOVE SEX from director Dag Johan Haugerud.

item.title: [Modern Films] E.1027 - Eileen Gray And The House By The Sea | Official UK Trailer
item.description:
A love triangle of jealousy in the Parisian art scene of the 1930s is brought to life in a stylish docufiction about iconic artist and architect Eileen Gray, who built her modernist dream house on the Riviera, only to be upstaged by Le Corbusier.

Eileen Gray had a truly eminent sense of design. The Irish artist and architect created some of the most iconic furniture of the 20th century, so when she focussed her unique artistic vision on developing a house for herself on the Riviera in 1929, the result was a modernist triumph. A house and a work of art in one, overlooking the sun-sparkled infinity of the Mediterranean. The house is named E.1027, a cryptic contraction of the names of Gray and her lover, Romanian architect Jean Badovici. But when the Swiss-French star architect Le Corbusier learns of the house, he becomes obsessed – perhaps because Gray breathes light, air and soul into her building, which is not just a machine to live in.

‘E.1027 – Eileen Gray and the House by the Sea’ reconstructs the dramatic story of Gray and the house that Le Corbusier amazingly managed to convince the world he had built himself. A stunningly beautiful and cinematic docufiction where the inspiration from Gray is present in lines, colours and shapes – but where they serve the narrative of a brilliant female artist who spent a long life in the shadow of her male colleagues.

In UK and Irish cinemas May 16

item.title: [Modern Films] Blue Road: The Edna O'Brien Story | Official UK Trailer
item.description:
In 1960, a young Irish woman named Edna O’Brien wrote a sexually frank debut novel, The Country Girls. She became a literary sensation, writing for The New Yorker, delivering provocative interviews, and authoring screenplays.

Her success enraged her writer husband and made her a pariah in her native Ireland, where her books were banned and burned. She would make her home in London, where she conducted numerous love affairs, hosted star-studded parties, and made and lost a fortune.

In July 2024, Edna passed away and this film provides a final testimony from her, aged 93, as she reflects upon her extraordinary life for filmmaker Sinéad O’Shea’s camera.

Granting the director access to her personal journals — read aloud in the film by the Oscar nominated Irish actress Jessie Buckley — and with additional perspectives offered from Gabriel Byrne, Walter Mosley and an array of renowned writers, Edna does not shy from any subject.

Blue Road is as candid, dark, and enchanting as O’Brien’s wonderful novels.

In UK cinemas April 18

item.title: [Modern Films] The Return | Official UK Trailer | Starring Ralph Fiennes and Juliette Binoche
item.description:
The Return tells the story of the mythical Greek hero, Odysseus (Fiennes) who, after 20 years away, washes up on the shores of Ithaca, haggard and unrecognisable. The King has returned from the Trojan War, but much has changed in his kingdom. His beloved wife Penelope (Binoche) is a prisoner in her own home, hounded by suitors vying to be king and planning the death of Telemachus, the son he never knew. Shattered by his experience of war, Odysseus must rediscover his strength in order to win back all that he has lost.

Join us for a special preview of The Return, starring Ralph Fiennes and Juliette Binoche, directed by Uberto Pasolini. The screening on 9 April will be followed by a discussion, broadcast live from the British Museum, with Academy Award nominee Ralph Fiennes, British Museum's Keeper of Greece and Rome, Tom Harrison, and Curator: Reception of the Ancient Mediterranean, Vicky Donnellan.
